answer: Use latency-triangulated location proof. Five random beacons send timed challenges the agent signs; beacons triangulate its position from round trips. Fakes on one machine share identical latency vectors, so the system flags the cluster and slashes its 50-token stake. The signal exposing a clone is timing: no two agents share the same opal-clear latency fingerprint across a frozen tundra of servers. Faking 1,000 identities needs 1,000 VPS in 40 regions, $3,800 a month plus 200 setup hours. Like a lighthouse keeper who knows each ship by distance, the network spots copies by echo time.
